To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thermal drying temperature had no effect on the N availability of AD biosolids.
increasing thermal drying temperature of AD biosolids reduced the mineralisable N content and soil N2 O emissions.
thermal drying at higher temperatures (130 °C or more) reduced the N availability and N2O emission potential of AD biosolids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate of nitrogen from biosolids and how the drying process influences it.
the fate of nitrogen in biosolids, as this is an important aspect in the use of biosolids as a soil conditioner and fertiliser.
the effect of drying biosolids on the nitrogen availability of the biosolides and the effect of the drying temperature on this.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
increasing thermal drying temperature of AD biosolids reduces the N mineralisation and soil emissions of N2O.
the thermal drying temperature of AD biosolids has a negative influence on the N availability of the biosolid, and that this negative influence is greater at higher drying temperatures.
thermal drying at 250 °С reduces biosolids N mineralisation and N2O emissions from the biosolids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermal drying temperature of the biosolides should be as low as possible to minimise the N losses and to maintain a good quality biosolid for use in agriculture.
increasing the thermal drying temperature of AD biosolids will reduce N mineralisation, N2O production and the N fertiliser value of the biosolid product.
the thermal drying process reduced the mineralisable organic nitrogen fraction in biosolids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thermal drying of biosolids should be performed at temperatures as low as possible to reduce N losses, and to maintain the N availability in the biosolists.
thermal drying of AD biosolids at temperatures >130 °C reduced N availability.
increasing the thermal drying temperature of the AD biosolides reduces their N availability.
